I will start from what has worked on my land and then adjust a little by crop price, water, and fertilizer cost. I have only 7.7 mu, so I cannot spread money everywhere without thinking. Since my main system is wheat-maize and I have well irrigation, I will keep most of the land in that rotation because it is steady and easier to manage for yield. Cotton can still stay on a smaller piece, but I will not expand it too much because cotton needs more watching, more spraying, and more labor over a long season. With my experience, I do not chase the lowest fertilizer rate. If I am uncertain, I would rather hold yield and spend a bit more on fertilizer than save a little money and lose production. For wheat, I will feed it enough base fertilizer plus one clear topdressing so I can push tillers and grain fill. For maize, I will put more nitrogen because maize responds fast when water is available. For cotton, I will keep fertilizer balanced and not let nitrogen run too high, otherwise it grows too much branch and is harder to manage. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it pays, irrigate on the key growth stages, and keep pesticide sprays to the practical number needed in a normal year.
